correctness.rationale: The optimal scalar constant follows from strict monotonicity of logarithmic elasticity (derivative contains u^2+2-2cosh u<0). Replacing the scalar inequality in the inspected published reverse-KL tensorization gives the nonlinear log-mgf inequality; Chernoff minimization yields c_p. Independent Bernoulli deficits and the exact binomial KL rate prove that any larger uniform tail exponent fails. The p=2 endpoint and p-downarrow-1 limit are addressed separately. The standalone deterministic program supplies 3600 checks but no finite computation is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The normalized exponent coefficient is the natural minimax invariant for an entire class of one-sided nonlinear heavy-tail concentration bounds. Determining its exact value and matching obstruction closes the global optimality question left by the motivating inequality. For p=3/2 the exponent improves from 1/3 to about 0.917935; the improvement factor tends to infinity as p decreases to one. This is more than a minor bound sharpening and it directly controls optimal confidence exponents for nonlinear statistics under the same assumptions.
